NMADTA

Network meta-analysis of multiple diagnostic tests

NMADTA brings Bayesian diagnostic-test network meta-analysis into R. Compare multiple tests using evidence from studies that evaluate different subsets of tests, with or without a gold standard reference test. Fit hierarchical or HSROC models, assess missing-data assumptions, and turn the results into posterior summaries and diagnostic accuracy plots.

Get started View on CRAN

Installation

Install JAGS 4.x first, then install the released package in R. NMADTA requires R 4.0.0 or later.

install.packages("NMADTA")
library(NMADTA)

The current release is 0.1.4. The installation guide includes a check that R can find JAGS.

A network of diagnostic evidence

The included dat.kang example combines 12 studies of deep vein thrombosis. Four compared D-dimer with venography, three compared ultrasonography with venography, and five compared D-dimer with ultrasonography. No study evaluated all three tests together.

NMADTA uses joint test-outcome counts within each study to compare the two candidate tests in one model. Venography is the reference standard; K = 2 counts the candidate tests.

data(dat.kang)

kang_fit <- nmadt.hierarchical(
  nstu = 12, K = 2,
  data = dat.kang,
  testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography"),
  directory = tempdir(),
  n.adapt = 5000, n.iter = 50000, n.chains = 3,
  conv.diag = TRUE
)

summary(kang_fit)
plot(kang_fit, type = "sroc")
SROC panels produced by NMADTA for D-dimer and ultrasonography in the 12-study example.

Actual NMADTA output from the worked example, using three chains and 50,000 iterations per chain. See the complete analysis for data preparation, numerical output, diagnostics, and reproducibility details.

Study-level diagnostic accuracy

The forest plots show study-level sensitivity and specificity for D-dimer and ultrasonography, using the same fitted model as the SROC display above. Points mark posterior medians, horizontal intervals show 95% credible intervals, and vertical dotted lines mark the pooled posterior medians.

plot(kang_fit, type = "forest")

Actual output from NMADTA 0.1.4 using the 12-study worked example. Dashed horizontal intervals identify studies in which that candidate test was not observed; these estimates are model-based. See the convergence assessment for this run. Click the figure to view it at full resolution.

Two model families, one workflow

Both model families return an nmadt object with common print(), summary(), and plot() methods.

Analysis Hierarchical model HSROC model
MAR formulation nmadt.hierarchical() nmadt.hsroc()
MNAR sensitivity analysis nmadt.hierarchical.MNAR() nmadt.hsroc.MNAR()

The hierarchical model directly parameterizes sensitivity and specificity. The HSROC model uses accuracy and threshold components. Read Choosing a model for the distinction and the assumptions that matter in practice.

Paper and replication

Xing X, Lu B, Lin L, Lian Q, Hodges JS, Chen Y, Chu H (2026). NMADTA: An R package for network meta-analysis of multiple diagnostic tests. Research Synthesis Methods. doi:10.1017/rsm.2026.10097.

The article describes the methods and software design and links to replication data and code. Its examples used NMADTA 0.1.3; this website documents version 0.1.4.
